To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new technique for heterodyne detection and demonstrated its use at 4.7 µm.
(a) we have measured the highest second-harmonic conversion efficiency of CO(2)-laser radiation in AgGaSe(3), and (b) we have demonstrated heterodyne detection with a 4.75-mm laser.

we have demonstrated the efficient generation of 4.7-µm light by second-harmonic conversion of CO(2)-laser radiation in AgGaSe( 2) and tellurium, and we have demonstrated heterodyne detection in this spectral region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient, tunable, and continuous sources of coherent 4- to 10-µ m radiation.
the development of efficient sources of 4.7-µm light, and with the development of heterodyne detection techniques for this wavelength region.
the efficient generation and detection of 4- to 6-µm radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work demonstrates that efficient generation of coherent radiation in the mid-infrared is possible by the use of nonlinear optical techniques, and that the detection of such radiation can be improved by heterodyne detection.
the authors are to be congratulated on their excellent experimental results and their careful analysis and interpretation of these results.
the results presented here represent an important step in the direction of making the 4.75-micron spectral region a useful region for spectroscopy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a 100-fold improvement in sensitivity for the detection of weak 4.75-microm radiation by using the heterodyne technique.
the generation and detection of coherent 4.75-micrometers radiation is feasible with present-day technology.
we have demonstrated the generation and detection of light in a spectral region that has been difficult to explore in the past.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficiency and power of the second-harmonic radiation generated by our 10.6-µm pump source are sufficient for the heterodyne detection and mixing of 4- to 10-µ m radiation with a sensitivity comparable to that of conventional infrared heterodyne receivers.

the use of the second harmonic as a local oscillator in heterodyne detection systems can be very advantageous, as it allows the use of the most efficient and most compact local oscillator source available, the cw laser, as well as a much more sensitive local oscillator than would otherwise be available.
efficient generation and heterodynes detection of 5 µm light is now possible.
